title: Gyoza
ingredients: 4 cups green cabbage, finely minced (about 1/2 a medium head)
1 tsp salt (for drawing moisture out of the cabbage)
1/2 tsp black pepper (no extra salt needed for the meat since the cabbage is pre-salted)
instructions: Mince: Finely chop or grate the cabbage into very small pieces (a food processor pulse works great).
Salt & Rest: Toss the minced cabbage in a bowl with 1 tsp of salt and let it sit for 10 to 15 minutes.
Squeeze: Grab handfuls of the cabbage and squeeze hard over the sink to wring out as much water as possible (or wring it out using a clean kitchen towel/cheesecloth).

In a large bowl, combine the ground pork, cabbage, chopped scallions, ginger, oyster sauce, soy sauce, sesame oil, cornstarch, and pepper. Mix vigorously in one direction with your hands or a fork for about 1–2 minutes until the mixture gets tacky and paste-like.

Set up a small bowl of water. Place a wrapper in your palm, add about 1 rounded teaspoon of filling to the center, and wet the top edge of the wrapper with water. Fold in half over the filling, pinching the edges tightly to seal. Make 3–4 pleats along one side as you press it closed to give it that classic crescent shape.
Steam, air fry, or pan fry
